stories.headline: Fuel truck fire on Cairo ring road kills at least 30
body: A vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Greater Cairo.
At least 30 people died and 25 were injured, Egypt's health ministry said.
Prosecutors have opened an investigation.
stories.vc: Road safety for fuel transport is a growing public concern.

stories.headline: Iraq's top court lets Baghdad take over Kurdish borders
body: Iraq's Federal Supreme Court ruled federal troops can deploy to all international borders, including in the Kurdish region.
It came a day after PM Ali al-Zaidi ordered forces to take over Kurdish-run crossings and oil fields to curb smuggling.
Kurdish authorities called the move an 'assault' on their rights.
stories.vc: Control of Kurdish oil affects Iraq's budget and regional oil supply.

stories.headline: Trump plans new tariffs on 14 economies, including India
body: The US plans new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, the EU and India.
It accuses them of using subsidies to overproduce and flood markets with cheap goods.
China faces the highest rates, after an eight-month investigation.
stories.joke: Tariffs: the gift that keeps on taxing.
stories.vc: Indian exporters may face higher costs selling to the US.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps over 2,000 points on foreign inflows and cheaper oil
body: The Sensex rose 2,062 points to a day's high of 84,498 on Wednesday; the Nifty hit 25,951.
Foreign fund buying, lower crude oil and bank stocks led the rally.
Brent crude fell 1.43% to about $90 a barrel.
stories.vc: Cheaper oil and foreign money lift Indian portfolios.

stories.headline: Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down as Flipkart CEO
body: Flipkart's CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down after more than 11 years.
A successor will be named in the coming weeks; tech chief Balaji Thiagarajan and the board will run things meanwhile.
The business grew more than fivefold under him.
stories.vc: Leadership change comes as Flipkart prepares for its next phase of growth.

stories.headline: Bengaluru's Blue Line metro trials begin from K.R. Puram
body: Trial runs have started on the first four stations of the Blue Line from K.R. Puram.
The 19-km stretch to Central Silk Board has 13 stations along the Outer Ring Road.
Public service is targeted for mid-2027.
stories.joke: Silk Board, your days are numbered.
stories.vc: Metro access along the ORR could ease commutes to tech parks.

stories.headline: FCC approves SpaceX's plan for AI data centres in space
body: The US FCC gave SpaceX conditional approval for up to 1 million satellites for orbital data centres.
Amazon, Viasat and astronomers objected over debris, interference and the environment.
Amazon called it 'a lofty ambition rather than a real plan'. (No new Unhedged episode, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: The cloud, now literally above the clouds.
stories.vc: Space data centres could reshape where AI computing gets built.

stories.statLabel: usage meter for Chat and Work
stories.headline: ChatGPT's heaviest users may hit limits sooner as Chat and Work merge
body: OpenAI is combining ChatGPT's Chat and Work modes with a single usage meter.
It's rolling out first to some Pro subscribers.
OpenAI says most users won't notice, but its heaviest users may. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.vc: Usage limits show how costly heavy AI use is to serve.

stories.headline: Dario Amodei rejects claims he wants AI to replace human control
body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called claims that he favours surrendering human free will to AI 'absurd'.
He wrote that handing governance to AI is 'a bad idea'.
Rivals had warned human agency is at risk. (No new Stratechery post, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: Humans stay in the driver's seat, for now.
stories.vc: AI safety debates shape regulation and investor risk.

stories.headline: PhonePe revives IPO plans for March 2027
body: Walmart-backed PhonePe has restarted talks with bankers for a March 2027 listing, sources told Inc42.
It may sell up to ₹12,000 crore of shares at a $12–15 billion valuation.
It paused its IPO in March citing global volatility. (TechCrunch Venture had no fresh deal, so this is Inc42's report.)
stories.vc: A PhonePe listing would be one of India's biggest fintech IPOs.

stories.headline: Lok Capital raises over $130M for its fifth impact fund
body: Lok Capital raised over $130 million in the first close of Fund V, targeting $200–250 million.
It will back 10–12 companies in financial inclusion and climate.
IFC, the European Investment Bank and FMO plan to invest. (No Economist piece was readable, so this is Inc42's report.)
stories.joke: Doing good, with a term sheet.
stories.vc: Impact funds bring growth money to businesses serving underserved Indians.

stories.headline: Lakshmi Venu sues for her share of Venu Srinivasan family assets
body: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of TVS Holdings chairman Venu Srinivasan, has asked the Madras High Court to split the family's joint assets.
Her lawyers say talks failed.
Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, backs her: 'a son and daughter are equal in every respect'.
stories.vc: Daughters' equal inheritance rights matter for women's wealth and business control.

stories.headline: Istanbul blocks a women's march despite court rulings
body: Istanbul authorities banned gatherings and blocked Taksim Square to stop a November 25 march against violence on women.
Courts had overturned similar bans in 2024 and 2025.
Organisers said they would march anyway.
stories.vc: Protest rights are key to pushing for laws that protect women.

stories.statLabel: orange flags, one per woman killed daily
stories.headline: UN deputy chief: 'far too much failure' on violence against women
body: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed called for justice for survivors and consequences for abusers.
Her event launched 16 Days of Activism against gender-based violence.
129 orange flags marked the women and girls killed by partners or family each day.
stories.vc: Justice that works for survivors helps women rebuild lives and careers.

stories.headline: Delhi to open two hospitals with 1,815 beds in 2027
body: CM Rekha Gupta said hospitals in Siraspur and Hastal, with 1,815 beds together, will open next year.
40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandir clinics will open in December.
She warned officials against delays.
stories.vc: New public beds ease pressure on Delhi's crowded big hospitals.

stories.headline: Himachal opens a 100-bed civil hospital in Kangra
body: CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu opened a new 100-bed Civil Hospital building at Shahpur in Kangra district.
It cost ₹11.50 crore.
He said staffing in state health centres has risen from 35% to nearly 70% of sanctioned posts.
stories.joke: Mountain views, now with a ward.
stories.vc: Local hospitals cut long trips to cities for hill communities.

stories.headline: Free heart hospital in Ahmedabad opens a 16-bed surgical ICU
body: Sri Sathya Sai Heart Hospital in Kasindra, Ahmedabad, opened a 16-bed advanced surgical ICU.
The hospital offers completely free treatment.
It has served Ahmedabad for eight years and Rajkot for 26.
stories.vc: More ICU beds mean more heart surgeries for patients who can't pay.

stories.headline: US futures watchdog posts record surplus as it halves its trade fee
body: The National Futures Association ended its fiscal year with a record $22.5 million surplus.
Most income comes from a fee on every futures trade, which rose with volumes.
It cut the fee from 2 cents to 1 cent per side for 12 months from July.
stories.vc: Lower per-trade fees matter most to high-volume traders.

stories.headline: LSEG and Tradeweb automate settlement of repo trades
body: LSEG and Tradeweb launched RepoAgent, which turns repo trades into settlement instructions automatically.
It starts with euro repo settling at Euroclear and Clearstream.
Tradeweb's repo platforms averaged $821.9 billion a day in October.
stories.vc: Automation cuts errors and costs after a trade is done.

stories.headline: Explainer: Why do tiny trading fees matter?
body: Imagine the school shop charges one paisa every time you buy or sell a sweet.
Grown-ups call this a per-trade fee, and 'per side' means both buyer and seller pay it.
This year, the group that oversees US futures cut its fee from 2 cents to 1 cent per side.
One cent sounds like nothing.
But fast traders make thousands of trades a day, so tiny fees add up to big money.
stories.vc: Fees shape which trades are worth doing.

stories.headline: Williams breached F1's 2025 cost cap and loses some wind tunnel time
body: Williams overspent F1's 2025 budget cap by £627,000, or 0.48%, the FIA said.
The FIA found it unintentional, but Williams loses 1.5% of its wind tunnel and CFD testing for 12 months.
Alpine was fined for a procedural breach.
stories.vc: Cost-cap rules aim to keep spending fair between rich and smaller teams.
